## Setup, global objects and dependencies

```{r}
#| label: packages

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
   DBI
  ,odbc
  ,dplyr
  ,dbplyr
  ,glue
  ,tidyverse
  ,gt
  ,ggplot2
  ,labelled
  ,sjlabelled
  ,hablar
  ,janitor
  ,scales
  )

pacman::p_load_gh("actepi/actepir")

# Non-default packages in use, for the dependency statement below
packs_loaded <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, sessionInfo()$otherPkgs))
packageslist <- as.data.frame(installed.packages()[, c(1, 3)]) |>
  dplyr::filter(Package %in% rownames(packs_loaded)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pl = paste0(Package, " (", Version, ")")) |>
  dplyr::pull(pl)

rm(packs_loaded)
```

<!-- BEGIN:conn -->
### Connection

```{r}
#| label: conn121

con121 <- DBI::dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  Driver = "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server",
  Server = "PRDSQL121vs.act.gov.au",
  Trusted_Connection = "Yes",
  Port = 1433
  )

invisible(gc())   # retain to clear sporadic Type 29 ODBC error
```

<!-- END:conn -->
<!-- BEGIN:sel -->
### Data selection

```{r}
#| label: selection

db <- "Analysis"    # leave alone
tb <- "TABLENAME"   # change to your required dataset

dt <- dplyr::tbl(con121, dbplyr::in_catalog(db, "dbo", tb)) |>
  # dplyr::filter() and dplyr::select() go here - the query stays lazy
  # until it reaches collect_withlabels()
  collect_withlabels()
```

<!-- END:sel -->
<!-- BEGIN:sql -->
### Data selection (SQL)

An alternative to the dbplyr route. Results are written to `dt_sql` rather than
`dt`, so both approaches can sit in the document while you decide which suits
the job.

```{sql}
#| label: selection-sql
#| connection: con121
#| output.var: dt_sql

SELECT TOP 100
       *
FROM   Analysis.dbo.TABLENAME
```
